sections.title: Overview
sections.body: Xploratory was a futures research initiative set up jointly by Koa Health and the Royal College of Art (RCA). The aim was to look beyond current product development and explore what mental wellbeing services and technologies could look like in 10 to 20 years. Rather than optimising existing products, the project asked more open questions: how will people's relationship with mental health change, what new contexts and behaviours will emerge, and what entirely new kinds of products might serve them?

sections.title: Why This Work Mattered
sections.body:
Product teams operating inside a company are necessarily focused on near-term delivery. Roadmaps, quarterly targets, and user feedback loops all pull attention towards incremental improvement. Futures work creates space for a different kind of thinking — one that is not constrained by current technology, business models, or user expectations.

For Koa Health, this was strategically important. Digital mental health was a fast-moving space with significant uncertainty about where regulation, clinical practice, and consumer behaviour were heading. Having a clearer view of plausible futures helped inform longer-term product strategy and investment decisions.

sections.title: The Process
sections.body:
Working with researchers and designers from the Royal College of Art, we ran a structured futures exploration process. This combined horizon scanning (tracking weak signals and emerging trends across technology, culture, healthcare policy, and social behaviour), expert interviews, and speculative design methods.

From this work we developed 33 distinct future scenarios, each describing a plausible context in which mental health and wellbeing services might operate. The scenarios varied widely — from near-future extensions of current trends to more speculative futures involving significant shifts in how society understands and manages mental health.

From these scenarios we then developed 10 future product concepts, each grounded in one or more of the scenarios. These ranged from passive monitoring systems that integrated into everyday environments, to new models for peer support and community-based care, to tools for preventative mental health management built into life transitions.

sections.title: Testing and Validation
sections.body: The product concepts were not just speculative sketches. We tested them with target users through an online study, collecting feedback on desirability, perceived value, and concerns. This gave the concepts empirical grounding and helped prioritise which directions were worth exploring further.

sections.title: My Role
sections.body: As VP of Product & Innovation at Koa Health, I initiated and oversaw the Xploratory programme, managed the collaboration with the Royal College of Art, and ensured the outputs were connected back to strategic decisions within the company. The work was published via the Xploratory website and contributed to Koa Health's positioning as a thought leader in the digital mental health space.
